section: Science · Ch41 — Matter & Materials — Deep Practice 2
subject: Science
stem: Which of the following is a chemical change, not a physical change?
explanation: Burning paper produces new substances (ash, gases) that cannot be reversed — a chemical change. Melting wax, dissolving sugar, and cutting wood are physical changes: no new substance forms, and most are reversible.

section: Science · Ch41 — Matter & Materials — Deep Practice 2
subject: Science
stem: Water (H₂O) is classified as a compound rather than a mixture because:

options.option_text: Hydrogen and oxygen combine in a fixed ratio and lose their individual properties
It can be separated by simple physical methods like filtration
Its composition varies depending on the sample
It retains the individual properties of hydrogen and oxygen gas

explanation: In a compound, elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio, forming a new substance with distinct properties (unlike its constituent elements) — unlike a mixture, whose composition can vary and be separated by physical means.

section: Science · Ch41 — Matter & Materials — Deep Practice 2
subject: Science
stem: Rubber is used to coat electrical wires mainly because it is a good:

options.option_text: Conductor, allowing current to pass through easily

explanation: Rubber is an insulator (poor conductor of electricity), so it safely contains the current within the wire, preventing shock to anyone touching the coating.
